title: The zero set of a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals on an affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals (a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal O_X$ which is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]). For $x\in X$ regard the stalk $\mathcal K_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] as an ideal of the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ (the map $\mathcal K_x\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ induced by the inclusion is injective, stalks being filtered colimits), and put $V(\mathcal K)=\{x\in X:\mathcal K_x\neq\mathcal O_{X,x}\}$. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, and identify $U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the point $x\in U$ corresponding to the prime $\mathfrak p_x\subset A$. Then for $x\in U$: $\mathcal K_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ if and only if $\mathcal K(U)\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_x$. That is, $V(\mathcal K)\cap U=V(\mathcal K(U))=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A:\mathcal K(U)\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$; consequently $V(\mathcal K)$ is a closed subset of $X$, and it is the underlying set of the closed subscheme of $X$ cut out by $\mathcal K$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf].

source.place: Schemes, Example 01HM (example-closed-subspace, line 369: the closed subspace associated to a sheaf of ideals I locally generated by sections has underlying set Z = Supp(O_X/I), i.e. the x with I_x != O_{X,x}, as in the proof of Lemma 01HP lemma-characterize-closed-subspace) with Lemma 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme, line 1744: on an affine open U = Spec R, i^{-1}(U) -> U is Spec(R/I) -> Spec R and I|_U = I~), so Z cap U = V(I(U)); the stalk computation (a in I(U) outside p_x is a unit near x; conversely 1 in K(D(f)) = K(U)_f forces f^m in K(U) subset p_x) is not written in Stacks
